A function is invertible if and only if it's a one-to-one function. To determine which of the functions are one-to-one, we use the horizontal line test.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/bfc7d94de67ceeb0c4aaa0988c117fce7f15242c2f3d223eecd8f0eb77135d7e.png)

From the above, we see that: 

- For graph IV, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line. Therefore, graph IV shows a one-to-one function. This means that  the function is invertible.

- For graphs I, II and  III, some horizontal lines intersect the curve more than once. So, these are not one-to-one functions. As a result, they are not invertible.
html:
A function is invertible if and only if it's a one-to-one function. To determine which of the functions are one-to-one, we use the horizontal line test.

From the above, we see that:

  • For graph IV, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line. Therefore, graph IV shows a one-to-one function. This means that the function is invertible.

  • For graphs I, II and III, some horizontal lines intersect the curve more than once. So, these are not one-to-one functions. As a result, they are not invertible.

Your Answer:
II and III only
